preview: AI and robotics are attracting growing investment in manufacturing, but that investment does not always mean the same thing for factories. In this episode, we look at where the change is taking place and ask what today’s spending can really tell us about the future of production.
comment_1: Listen for the difference between what companies plan to do and what they are already doing.
comment_2: So far, companies are planning to use more AI and robots, but most are not using highly independent machines yet. As you listen, ask: Is this investment making factories more independent, or is it also supporting other parts of the AI economy?
comment_3: The main message is simple: interest in AI and robots is growing faster than their use in everyday factory work. At the same time, this change is not happening in only one place or in only one way. Now let’s look more closely at these two sides.
comment_4: So, the picture is more specific than the headline numbers suggest. Robots are being used in some sectors, and the AI boom may also appear in the industries that support it, not only on factory production lines. Now let’s bring these points together and look at the bigger picture.
